texts.facts: 2. The first respondent herein, who is a resident within the limits of Vengola Grama Panchayat, the third respondent herein, has approached this Court in W.P. (C)No.31959 of 2018 seeking a writ of mandamus commanding respondents 2 to 4 herein to stop all meat and fish stalls on the side of Perumbavoor - Puthenkuruz road near Pathipalam, conducting illegal trade and exhibition of fish and meat in violation of the direction issued by this Court. He has also sought for a writ of mandamus commanding the third and fourth respondents herein not to issue any licence to the meat and fish stalls conducted illegally in Vengola Grama Panchayat in the light of the Judgment of this Court in Mather v. Valakom Grama Panchayat (2009 (3) KLT 572); and also a writ of mandamus commanding the third and fourth respondents herein to consider and take action on Ext.P6 representation preferred by him, within a time limit to be fixed by this Court. 3. In the writ petition, it is averred that the petitioner is residing in Vengola Grama Panchayat and his house is situated on the side of Perumbavoor - Puthenkuruz road. In front of the petitioner's property, there are several unauthorised meat and fish stalls, which are conducted without any Shameer M.V vs Aju Thomas on 19 November, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87085733/ 3 licence. The document marked as Ext.P1 series is photographs of such meat and fish stalls. The residents in the locality submitted Ext.P2 complaint dated 14.08.2017 and the third respondent Grama Panchayat convened a joint meeting on 13.10.2017 of the residents, traders, representatives of political parties, etc. The document marked as Ext.P4 is a news report that appeared in Mathrubhumi daily dated 20.09.2017 regarding the complaints raised against the meat and fish stalls at Pathipalam. Based on a complaint made by the petitioner, the Secretary of the Grama Panchayat, the fourth respondent herein, issued Ext.P5 notice dated 19.07.2017 for conducting a personal hearing on 20.07.2017. Thereafter, the petitioner submitted Ext.P6 representation dated 26.07.2018 before the Health Inspector of the Grama Panchayat, the fifth respondent herein, with a request to take necessary action against unauthorised meat and fish stalls in Ward No.IX of Vengola Grama Panchayat. 4. On 15.10.2018, when W.P.(C)No.31959 of 2018 came up for consideration, the learned Standing Counsel for Vengola Grama Panchayat submitted that fish and meat vending is conducted without securing license/permit. Since Ext.P6 representation is pending consideration, the learned Single Judge disposed of the writ petition by directing the Health Inspector of the Grama Panchayat, the fifth respondent herein, to take an appropriate action on the basis of Ext.P6 at the earliest, at any rate, within one month from the date of receipt of a copy of that judgment. It was made clear that, if the Secretary of the Grama Panchayat finds any difficulty in implementing the order, he will be at liberty to seek necessary Police aid for that purpose, and if any request is so made, the Police authorities shall take adequate steps. 5. In W.P.(C)No.31959 of 2018, none of the fish/meat vendors on the side of Perumbavoor - Puthenkuruz road near Pathipalam are arrayed as respondents. The appellants, who are conducting meat/fish business at Pathipalam would contend that they came to know about the judgment dated 15.10.2018 of the learned Single Judge only when they were issued with a closure notice dated 03.11.2018 of the fourth respondent Secretary and that, they are unaware of the directions stated to have been issued by the Grama Panchayat on 26.10.2018, 21.10.2018 and 31.10.2018 to close down their shops. They were never given an opportunity of being heard prior to the issuance of the closure notice dated 03.11.2018. Along with the writ appeal, the appellants have produced certain documents as Annexures A1 to A26 in order to show that they are having registration under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, Sanitation Certificate from Community Health Centre, Vengola, etc. and that their applications for D&O Licence are pending consideration before the Grama Panchayat. The document marked as Annexure A27 is the closure notice dated 03.11.2018 issued to the fourth appellant. The grievance of the appellants, who are third parties to W.P.(C)No.31959 of 2018, is that they came to know about the judgment dated 15.10.2018 of the learned Single Judge only when they were issued with a closure notice dated 03.11.2018 of the fourth respondent Secretary of the Grama Panchayat, whereby the fish/meat vendors at Pathipalam are directed to close down their shops within three days. According to the appellants, they were not afforded with an opportunity of being heard before the issuance of the closure notice dated 03.11.2018. The writ petition was disposed of without the fish/meat vendors at Pathipalam in the party array. Now, without giving them an opportunity of being heard, a closure notice dated 03.11.2018 has been issued by the fourth respondent Secretary of the Grama Panchayat. texts.arguments: 8. In Prabodh Verma v. State of U.P. [(1984) 4 SCC 251] a Three-Judge Bench of the Apex Court held that a High Court ought not to hear and dispose of a writ petition under Article 226 of the Constitution without the persons who would be vitally affected by its judgment being before it as respondents or at least some of them before it as respondents in a representative capacity, if their number is too large to join them as respondents individually, and, if the petitioners refuse to so join them the High Court ought to dismiss the petition for non-joinder of necessary parties. The learned counsel for the first respondent/writ petitioner, during the course of arguments, has not disputed the fact that the closure notice dated 03.11.2018 is one issued by the fourth respondent Secretary of the Grama Panchayat, without affording the appellants and other traders an opportunity of being heard.
texts.petitioner_arguments: The learned counsel for the first respondent/writ petitioner, during the course of arguments, has not disputed the fact that the closure notice dated 03.11.2018 is one issued by the fourth respondent Secretary of the Grama Panchayat, without affording the appellants and other traders an opportunity of being heard.
